text:
alex: heads-up — ran nsys on nightly inference-run (dedicated pool) and saw repeated peaks at ~120ms intervals in the timeline. looks like a harmonic resonance across attention kernels. attaching perfetto: https://perfetto.google.com/trace?session=2749991112
perf-bot: uploaded trace to GCS: gs://redwood-traces/2749991112/nsys-perfetto.pb :white_check_mark:
maya: curious — single layer alignment or multi-layer synchronous spikes? did we change kernel selection in last deploy?
jon: quick dump from the nsys sampling summary (top by total GPU time):
```
1) aten::multi_head_attention_forward_fwd - 44.2s
2) cuda_launch_attn_kv - 21.8s
3) kv_cache_prefetch - 9.3s
4) layernorm_forward_cuda - 4.6s
5) softmax_attn_cuda - 3.9s
```
jon: interestingly, the attn_kv kernel shows periodic high-latency invocations rather than a constant tail.
lina: could be batching cadence + KV cache eviction dance; we recently tuned packer to flush earlier for latency targets.
maya: can someone post SM util / L2 traffic counters from the same trace? need to correlate.
alex: added perfetto flame with SM occupancy overlay (see main link). note: attn bursts line up with KV cache thrash events and ~4MB transient L2 bandwidth spikes.
jon: small spectral analysis: timeline shows harmonics at ~8 Hz and multiples. suggests aligned fetch/evict across warps/streams -> amplified stalls.
lina: theory: the micro-batch flush optimization moved a flush boundary to earlier in the loop so multiple streams flush near-simultaneously, causing aligned KV fetches and L2 pressure.
alex: repro steps: export BATCHER_DEBUG=1; set BATCH_MAX_SEQ=1024; run synthetic 1k rps job against nightly model; reproduce within ~30s.
maya: mitigation idea: introduce a tiny random jitter (10-30ms) to batch flush timing to de-synchronize. also consider a staggered KV fetch window or staggered kernel launch offsets.
jon: tried jitter locally: re-ran nsys for same workload with jitter=20ms; results: total attn kernel time -18%, SM occupancy more diffuse (was 48% spikey -> 62% steady), warp stall reason shifted from 'memory' dominance to 'execution' a bit.
perf-bot: scheduled perf run with jitter flag enabled: https://perfetto.google.com/trace?session=2749991388 (uploaded)
alex: good. action items: (1) revert the micro-batch flush optimization until we have a deeper fix, (2) add a runtime flag for batcher jitter to deploy to staging, (3) add automated nsys smoke when scheduler/micro-batching code changes.
maya: I'll open a PR for the jitter flag + a short perf job in CI to capture SM/L2 counters on changes.
lina: I'll draft a short runbook note on how to triage harmonic spikes (include spectral check, L2 transient scan, and KV prefetch cadence).
alex: thx everyone. let’s keep the perf traces linked in the PR and tag @eng-runtime for any further regressions. :thumbsup:
